question: Which published claims are stamped `documented`?
method: records with kind=wire and stamp=documented. `documented` maps to the prose tier `documented_fact`; the stamp governs how the claim may be restated, not how important it is.

The Indianapolis Department of Public Works reopened the city's floodgates on Sunday 16 August 2026 after the White River peaked early that morning, urging residents to be cautious as they returned to flood-damaged neighbourhoods while emergency shelters remained open.

Trump has directed the Pentagon to reduce the scale of joint military exercises with South Korea.
Trump announced the decision in a social media post, saying the exercises slated to begin this week are costly.
South Korea's president has proposed talks with Pyongyang aimed at formally ending the Korean War and replacing the armistice.

Trump's announcement came a day after the United States pulled its last aircraft carrier in Asia, with the USS George Washington sent to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Persian Gulf, NBC News reported on 16 August 2026.

North Korea on Friday 14 August 2026 threatened unspecified stern steps against the United States and South Korea, describing the drills as a rehearsal for an aggressive war that was triggering greater instability in the region.

US and South Korean forces were expected to practise joint operations in complex scenarios during Ulchi Freedom Shield, including a live-fire exercise testing joint precision targeting and manoeuvre, a wet gap crossing, and distribution of prepositioned military equipment.

Earlier in August 2026 South Korea, the United States and Japan detected the launch of a short-range ballistic missile from North Korea, the North's first ballistic weapons testing activity since late June, which landed in waters off its east coast.

The joint exercises come days after South Korea, the United States and Japan detected the second North Korean missile test in days, part of ballistic missile testing this month that is banned by the United Nations.

Trump has sought to curtail the exercises before, suspending them entirely in 2018 during denuclearisation negotiations with Kim Jong Un, and the drills were scaled back again in 2020 during the Covid-19 pandemic.

After his 2018 meeting with Kim Jong Un in Singapore, Trump told reporters the United States would be stopping the war games to save a tremendous amount of money, unless and until future negotiations were not going as they should.

Trump's 16 August 2026 announcement came a day after he posted a photo of himself standing next to Kim Jong Un, writing that the two leaders get along great despite the unfriendly look in that particular picture.

Trump met the North Korean leader three times during his first term to discuss the country's nuclear programme, most recently in 2019, and has expressed interest in continuing those discussions since returning to office.
The Hill reported on 16 August 2026 that Trump said in a Truth Social post that he had told Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to substantially reduce the joint military exercises with South Korea.

South Korea's military said it fired warning shots after North Korean soldiers briefly crossed the military demarcation line, an incident that forced the North Korean soldiers to retreat, according to Reuters and Yonhap reporting dated 16 August 2026.

South Korea's President Lee proposed talks with Pyongyang on formally ending the Korean War and replacing the 1953 armistice with peace, a proposal Pyongyang snubbed as inter-Korean tensions flared ahead of the US-South Korea drills.
The State of New Mexico sued the Justice Department and Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia over withheld Epstein records.
The stated federal rationale for the 2019 stand-down request was avoiding the risk that parallel investigations would produce inconsistent statements exploitable by defence counsel.
Jeffrey Epstein died in federal custody on 10 August 2019, ending the federal prosecution.

Zorro Ranch, roughly 8,000 acres in Santa Fe County, was sold at public auction in 2023 to San Rafael Ranch LLC, an entity registered with the New Mexico Secretary of State roughly one month before the purchase.
The ownership of San Rafael Ranch LLC was not disclosed at purchase and became public only after a street-name change and a contested property-tax assessment prompted public-records requests.
The owner is Don Huffines, a former Texas state senator now running for Texas Comptroller; his wife Mary Catherine is listed as a trustee and his son Colin as an LLC manager.
New Mexico reopened its criminal investigation on 19 February 2026, after the Justice Department's January 2026 release of the Epstein files.
State and county officials ordered construction at the property paused, alleging the owners failed to obtain required permits.
The owners intend to convert the property into a Christian retreat.
New Mexico's Touhy letter of 3 May 2026 requested a response by 11 May 2026. The suit was filed on 5 August 2026, 86 days after that date passed.

The suit is docketed as No. 1:26-cv-02762-AHA in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, assigned to Judge Amir H. Ali, and is pleaded as review of agency action under the Administrative Procedure Act rather than as a FOIA case.

The records New Mexico seeks are the redacted materials in the federal 'Epstein Library', compiled under Section 2(a)(1)-(9) of the Epstein Files Transparency Act, Public Law 119-38 (19 November 2025).

New Mexico gave the federal government its entire investigative file — police reports, recorded witness interviews and materials on Epstein's use of state public lands — on 17 September 2019, after agreeing to stand down.

New Mexico's filing notes that the Justice Department has argued in other 2026 litigation that courts may take judicial notice of an Acting Attorney General's recorded public statements as binding party admissions.

The complaint states that federal law enforcement never searched Zorro Ranch, and cites a federal email of 23 August 2019 — thirteen days after Epstein's death — that acknowledged a victim who may have been raped at the New Mexico residence while asserting there was no probable cause to search it.

The federal district office's response, dated 30 June 2026 and delivered 14 July, stated it had neither collected nor retained investigative materials; the thirty-one accompanying pages consisted largely of a public news article, a public press release by a former governor, correspondence New Mexico had itself sent, and a list of follow-up questions.

New Mexico states it is investigating potential felony offences including homicide, kidnapping, criminal sexual penetration, criminal sexual contact and human trafficking, under named provisions of the New Mexico criminal code.

Asked whether the federal government would join New Mexico in seeking a modification of the protective orders it cited as the obstacle, so that the orders would expressly permit disclosure for law-enforcement purposes, a Deputy United States Attorney responded that such cooperation was 'unlikely' and identified no path through which the two offices could work together.

The federal filing states the released Epstein Files contain more than 13,000 references to Zorro Ranch and more than 5,000 references to New Mexico as locations where victims were trafficked, groomed and assaulted.
The state's own formal request dates its search of the property to 9 March 2026.
Then-Attorney General Hector Balderas asked the federal government on 15 October 2019 to begin seizing Epstein's New Mexico land holdings for the benefit of survivors.
The complaint dates the federal stand-down request to a telephone call on 23 July 2019 and cites a federal record of that call in the publicly released Epstein Files.

The federal government asked New Mexico to file the formal Touhy request it later declined: on 1 April 2026 an Associate Deputy Attorney General affirmed the Department's commitment to assisting and requested that New Mexico submit a Touhy letter through standard channels.

Gov. Josh Green said at least one person died in a car accident in the South Point area of the Big Island, while 19 roofs were lost and 190 flights were postponed as Hurricane Lala passed on 15 August 2026.

Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines cancelled 54 inter-island flights and 11 trans-Pacific flights on Saturday 15 August 2026 because of the storm, with five of the cancelled trans-Pacific flights to or from Kona.

The National Hurricane Center issued a rare hurricane warning for Hawaii's Big Island on Saturday 15 August 2026, where a landfall would have been the first in 155 years, with forecasters predicting up to 25 inches of rain at higher elevations.
